root_cause.text: The `driver_override` string in the AP device structure was accessed without locking in `__ap_revise_reserved()` and related functions, allowing a concurrent `driver_override_store()` to free the string while it was being read, leading to a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: Commit message explicitly states: "When the AP masks are updated via apmask_store() or aqmask_store(), ap_bus_revise_bindings() is called after ap_attr_mutex has been released. This calls __ap_revise_reserved(), which accesses the driver_override field without holding any lock, racing against a concurrent driver_override_store() that may free the old string, resulting in a potential UAF." Patch replaces custom `driver_override` field with the driver-core infrastructure that uses an internal spinlock for protection.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit d38a87d7c0643db61e7a3bfc3ebeea2dc2568f7e
Author: Harald Freudenberger <freude@linux.ibm.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 19 16:27:36 2025 +0100

    s390/ap: Support driver_override for AP queue devices
    
    Add a new sysfs attribute driver_override the AP queue's
    directory. Writing in a string overrides the default driver
    determination and the drivers are matched against this string
    instead. This overrules the driver binding determined by the
    apmask/aqmask bitmask fields.
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces `driver_override` string access in multiple functions without any locking. In `__ap_revise_reserved()`, `ap_dev->driver_override` is read and compared via `strcmp()` without holding a lock (line: `if (strcmp(ap_dev->driver_override, ap_drv->driver.name))`). Similarly, `ap_owned_by_def_drv()` reads `aq->ap_dev.driver_override` without locking (line: `bool override = !!aq->ap_dev.driver_override;`), and `ap_device_probe()` does the same (line: `if (ap_dev->driver_override)`). This allows a concurrent `driver_override_store()` to free the string while it is being read, leading to a use-after-free. No fix (locking) is present in this commit.
